subject: Renewal forecast — proactive stress test for Acme Retail (Q3 commit)
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal forecast — proactive stress test for Acme Retail (Q3 commit)

Team,

I ran a quick stress test on Acme Retail's renewal this morning and flagged a potential shortfall if they push payments or pause a module. I attached the model I used (acme-forecast-stress-test.xlsx).

Ask: can each of you confirm the following by EOD today?
- Ben: update the commit column in the attached sheet with last confirmed PO amounts and any verbal confirms.
- Naomi: quick check on open procurement redlines and whether finance has sign-off on our proposed 30/60 payment split.

Quick context: Acme indicated budget tightening in Q3 in the last call. We need to avoid being surprised in the forecast close — if the commit drops below $650k we trigger a finance escalation.

Also please tag any accounts with renewal-risk=high in HubSpot (link below) so RevOps can apply the correct coverage.

Thanks — I want a concise, defensible number for the finance commit meeting on Monday.

— Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: acme-forecast-stress-test.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/ACME-7821
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Apr 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal forecast — proactive stress test for Acme Retail (Q3 commit)

Good notes — updated the attached commit log (acme-commit-log.csv) and the stress test workbook with two scenarios: conservative (buyer asks for 30% deferral) and baseline (on schedule).

Summary:
- Baseline committed ARR: $710,000 (POs on file for core and analytics modules)
- Conservative scenario: $585,000 (analytics module delayed; buyer asking to push one invoice)
- Confirmed verbal from Josh M. for renewal but awaiting PO signature on the final line item for analytics (expected Tue morning).

Action items:
- I flagged the analytics module as renewal-risk=medium-high in HubSpot and left a note with the last conversation time.
- If we need to maintain a $650k commit level for finance, we should prioritize closing the analytics PO or propose a partial invoice now.

Quoted for context:
> On Sun, 22 Apr 2028 at 09:12, Stephanie Nguyen wrote:
> > Team,
> > I ran a quick stress test on Acme Retail's renewal this morning...

— Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme-commit-log.csv (csv, 4KB)
From: Josh Miller <josh.miller@acme-retail.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Apr 2028 17:28:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Renewal forecast — proactive stress test for Acme Retail (Q3 commit)

Thanks for the heads up — appreciate the transparency. Quick reality check from our side: finance is running a tighter cash flow this quarter and they've asked us to look at smoothing large vendor payments. We remain committed to Redwood but need flexibility on timing.

Proposal from Acme Finance:
- Approve the renewal at the full scope, but split the analytics module invoice 50/50 across two months (May/June).
- Sign the PO this week to lock pricing, then we submit a payment plan to Acme Finance.

If that works, we believe we can keep the overall renewal intact and avoid a formal reduction. Can Redwood provide a short amendment (1-pager) to document the payment split? We can loop procurement.

Thanks,
Josh Miller
Director, IT Procurement
Acme Retail

On Sun, Apr 22, 2028 at 11:04 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com> wrote:

Date: Mon, 23 Apr 2028 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal forecast — proactive stress test for Acme Retail (Q3 commit)

Looping back after a quick call with Finance.

Plan we can execute this week:
- Ben: please log the confirmed PO signature when you receive it and mark the HubSpot record with renewal-status=signed (even if payment plan follows).
- Stephanie: draft the 1-page amendment that formalizes a 50/50 split on the analytics invoice and a payment schedule. I can push this to Legal for a fast-track review.
- I will ask RevOps to temp-tag this deal as "payment-plan" so forecasting excludes the second invoice from the immediate commit number; finance will treat the first 50% as committed ARR for this quarter.

We should target finishing the amendment and obtaining PO signature by Tue EOD. If we meet that, the forecast shortfall disappears in the baseline. If not, escalate to Finance for guidance at the weekly review.

Next steps:
- Stephanie to upload amendment draft to the HubSpot deal (link) and set the DocuSign route to Josh.
- Ben to confirm PO + upload scanned PO to the deal.
- Naomi will notify FP&A of the temporary adjustment to commit numbers.

— Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Financial Analyst, Revenue Finance
Redwood Inference
